name: MAX7219 CNG
notes: 8-digit 7-segment LED display driver, SPI, multiplexed. Cascadable. CNG = 24-pin DIP commercial temp.
qs: How many in stock?

name: MAX7221 CNG
notes: Same silicon as MAX7219 but true SPI and lower EMI. Use when sharing a bus with other SPI devices.
qs: How many in stock?

name: ADC0804 LCJ
notes: 8-bit SAR ADC, parallel out, single channel, ~100us conversion (10 kS/s). Needs external clock + 5 V ref. Too slow/coarse for the MAF scope; fine for slow sensors.
qs: Confirm suffix (LCJ vs LCJ-1) and clock source plan

name: TDA7052
notes: 1.2 W mono audio amp, BTL output - speaker connects across two pins, NEVER ground either terminal. 3-18 V supply. Candidate for YM2612 audio output stage.

name: 74HCT154N
notes: 4-to-16 line decoder/demux. HCT = TTL thresholds so 3.3 V drives cleanly. Two enables. Directly usable for ISA bridge address decode. qty 3 (photo).

name: DM74150N
notes: 16-input multiplexer (data selector), NOT a microprocessor as some captions claim. 4-bit address, inverted output, active-low strobe. National Semiconductor.

name: 74LS153
notes: Dual 4-input multiplexer, shared address lines, separate enables.
Hex inverter buffer/driver, open-collector 30 V outputs. Needs pull-ups. Workhorse for driving relays/lamps.

name: 74LS161
notes: 4-bit synchronous binary counter, async clear, loadable, cascadable. Useful for ISA wait-state timing.

name: Z80A CPU
notes: 8-bit CPU, 4 MHz version. Full bus (A0-A15, D0-D7, /MREQ, /IORQ, /RD, /WR). Enables a historically-correct ISA host: Z80 firmware instead of PIC32 pretending. Needs clock, reset, ROM/RAM.
qs: Do we have a 4 MHz clock source / crystal?
Any Z80 peripheral chips (PIO, SIO, CTC) in stock?

name: LM324N
notes: Quad op-amp, single supply 3-32 V, inputs to ground. Not rail-to-rail out (~1.5 V from each rail). Four poles of active filter in one package - the right part for the MAF filter if we go active.

name: 7812 regulator
notes: Fixed +12 V linear, ~1 A with heatsink. Needs ~14.5 V+ in. Dissipates (Vin-12)*I as heat.

name: 74LS139
notes: Dual 2-to-4 decoder/demux, active-low outputs. Smaller partner to the 154.

name: 74S157
notes: Quad 2-input multiplexer, Schottky (fast, more power). Selects between two 4-bit sources.

name: SN7448N
notes: BCD to 7-segment decoder/driver, active-high outputs, open-collector with pull-ups.

name: NTE2021
notes: NTE generic substitute, believed 7406-class hex buffer. NTE numbers do NOT map to original part numbers - check the NTE datasheet.
qs: Confirm from NTE datasheet

name: NTE1904
notes: Unidentified NTE part. NTE numbering is proprietary - must look up.
qs: Look up NTE1904 datasheet

name: 741 op-amp
notes: Classic general-purpose op-amp. Slow (1 MHz GBW), not rail-to-rail, not suited to audio or precision work. LM324 is the better choice for most tasks here.

name: NTE74LS175
notes: Quad D flip-flop with clear, LS logic (NTE equivalent of 74LS175). Useful for latching, register storage, debounce.
qs: Confirm pinout matches 74LS175 standard

name: TL082 Dual BiFET Op-Amp
notes: Dual JFET-input op-amp. High input impedance (1e12 ohm), 3 MHz GBW, slew 13 V/us - much faster than the 741. Dual supply typically +/-15 V but works at +/-5 V. JFET inputs suit high-impedance sensors and audio; not rail-to-rail out.
qs: Which is better for the MAF filter: TL082 (JFET, fast) or LM324 (single supply, quad)?

name: 5W 0.33 ohm wirewound resistor
notes:
Decode: 5W = 5 watt, R33 = 0.33 ohm, J = +/-5%. Twenty in stock.

Useful for: current sensing (0.33 ohm x 15 A = 4.95 V - good range for shunt sensing), emitter degeneration, ballast, dummy load, LED current limiting at high current.

CAUTION: at 5 W into 0.33 ohm, I(rms) = sqrt(P/R) = 3.9 A continuous. Above that it cooks. Short pulses allow much more.
qs: What is this batch intended for - shunt sensing, or dummy load?
